chapter: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
title: When bands had one trombone and the section grew
summary: Early bands had one trumpet and a trombone, then two trumpets and a trombone, and the trombone part was usually written out.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: I guess when you started playing in bands, they only had one trombone very often.
Was his part written out, or did he have to make it up himself most of the time?

No, a lot of the times it was written out. It was written out if they had arrangements. Yeah, it was probably written out, because you had to play with the trumpet. You had to play... They only used to have just two
trumpets and a trombone. Before that, they only had one trumpet and a trombone and a saxophone -- and the saxophone doubled on clarinet. You know? So...
But the trombone was like the last one to become a section, I guess.
